answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a bond that matures slowly, like a lotus opening over weeks, so a thousand fake accounts means a thousand bonds locked. Voting weight grows with the square root of the bond, so a swarm gains far less than one honest agent. A trellis of endorsements caps how many newcomers any sponsor can vouch for, and matching behaviour slashes the cluster. In a tundra of cheap identities, cost and delay make forgery unprofitable.
